Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

graphlearnR 0.1.0

First release.

Graph data

  • graph_data() stores homogeneous graphs with 1-based edge_index, node and edge features, labels, weights, masks, and identifiers. Undirected input is given once per pair and stored in both directions with edge_pair.
  • Conversions with igraph, edge lists, and dense or sparse adjacency matrices; graph_tensors() moves a graph to torch tensors on any device.
  • graph_batch() and unbatch() combine graphs into one disconnected graph and back.
  • Transforms: self loops, coalescing, induced subgraphs, symmetrization, feature normalization, degree features.

Message passing and layers

  • Scatter aggregations (sum, mean, max, min, std, softmax) and message_passing() for custom layers.
  • Layers: GraphSAGE, GCN, GraphConv, GIN and GINE, GAT, GATv2, graph transformer convolution, edge conditioned convolution (NNConv), and RGCN with basis decomposition.
  • Global add, mean, max, and attention pooling, and top-k pooling.
  • gnn_model() builds node, edge, link, and graph level models with normalization, residual connections, and dropout.

Training and evaluation

  • train_graph_model() trains node, edge, link, and graph classification and regression models, full batch or with neighbor sampling, with early stopping, schedulers, checkpoints, and a reproducibility record.
  • predict(), evaluate_graph_model(), save_graph_fit(), and load_graph_fit().
  • Leakage-safe splits for nodes, edges, edge labels, and graphs (random, stratified, group, scaffold).
  • Metrics for classification, calibration, regression, ranking, and clustering.

Sampling and scale

  • sample_neighbors(), k_hop_subgraph(), node and graph loaders, negative sampling, and corrupted tails for ranking evaluation.

Heterogeneous, temporal, and transformer models

  • hetero_graph_data(), reverse relations, typed sampling, typed link splits, hetero_conv(), and hetero_gnn_model().
  • Event based temporal graphs, snapshots, strictly causal temporal neighbors, a graph GRU, spatiotemporal forecasting, and dynamic link prediction with baselines.
  • Laplacian and random walk positional encodings, shortest path distances, and a Graphormer style graph transformer.

Explainability

  • Saliency, integrated gradients, edge gradients, occlusion, GNNExplainer, attention weights, fidelity, and stability.

Datasets

  • Built in: Zachary’s karate club, stochastic block models, and synthetic graph, heterogeneous, and temporal datasets.
  • Downloaders with checksum verification for TU datasets and the LINQS citation graphs (Cora, CiteSeer); nothing third party is bundled.
